stem: A nurse discovers that a medication error was intercepted before the medication reached the client. What is the appropriate nursing response to this near miss?

options.A: Acknowledge and document the near miss according to the organization's safety-reporting process
options.B: Do not report it because no medication reached the client and no injury occurred
options.C: Delete any record of the event so the near miss does not affect unit quality data
options.D: Report it only if the same error later reaches a client and causes harm

rationale: The 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan explicitly includes acknowledging and documenting practice errors and near misses within Safety and Infection Prevention and Control. A near miss does not become irrelevant merely because harm was prevented. Therefore A is the best response; suppressing the event or waiting for future harm conflicts with the nurse's safety responsibilities.
educational_objective: Respond to a near miss by acknowledging and documenting it through the appropriate safety-reporting process even when no client harm occurred.
source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
source_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control, printed p.25-26 / PDF p.29-30: acknowledge and document practice errors and near misses; protect clients and health care personnel from hazards
source_claim_supported: The RN is expected to acknowledge and document practice errors and near misses as part of client safety practice.

correction_summary: Replaced an abstract AHRQ systems-analysis statement with the direct 2026 NCSBN action expected of an entry-level RN after a near miss. Corrected the category from Management of Care to Safety and Infection Prevention and Control and removed claims about near misses necessarily having the same systemic vulnerabilities as harmful errors.
audit_findings: A directly matches the NCSBN activity statement. B, C, and D incorrectly condition reporting/documentation on actual client harm. The item tests a clear RN action with no dependence on the specific causal-analysis framework used by a facility. No second-answer ambiguity, cueing, unsupported precision, or unresolved conflict remains.
